name: The Sacraments: Baptism and the Lord's Supper
path: Ecclesiology: The Doctrine of the Church

objectives.text: Identify baptism and the Lord's Supper as the two sacraments Jesus gave to his church
Name water as the sign used in baptism and bread and wine as the signs used in the Lord's Supper
Recall that Jesus commanded his disciples to baptize in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit
Retell the account of Jesus giving the bread and the cup to his disciples on the night he was betrayed
Explain that the sacraments are signs that point to Christ and what he has done for his people
Define a sacrament, using the Westminster Shorter Catechism, as a holy ordinance instituted by Christ in which visible signs represent, seal, and apply Christ and his benefits to believers
Explain what baptism signifies, including washing from sin and union with Christ in his death and resurrection
Explain what the Lord's Supper shows forth, including the proclamation of Christ's death and the spiritual nourishment of believers
Explain how circumcision and the Passover served as Old Testament signs of the covenant that anticipate baptism and the Lord's Supper
Compare baptism and the Lord's Supper in how often each is received, what each signifies, and to whom each is given
Describe the self-examination Scripture calls for before coming to the Lord's Supper, including knowledge to discern the Lord's body, faith, repentance, love, and new obedience
Describe how the Westminster Larger Catechism calls Christians to improve their baptism throughout life and identify the Scripture it draws on
Explain how the Lord's Supper expresses believers' communion with Christ and with one another as one body
Explain the distinction between the sign and the thing signified and why Scripture can speak of the sign by the name of what it signifies
Explain the Reformed teaching that Christ is truly but spiritually present in the Lord's Supper and is received by faith
Explain the Reformed position that baptism is to be administered both to those who profess faith and to the infants of believing parents, tracing its basis in covenant continuity
Explain how the sacraments become effectual not by any power in themselves or in the one who administers them but by the blessing of Christ and the work of his Spirit
Distinguish worthy from unworthy receiving of the Lord's Supper and explain the consequences Scripture attaches to each
Analyze how the sacraments function as means of grace that confirm the faith the Holy Spirit works through the preaching of the Word
Analyze why the Reformed tradition recognizes only two sacraments by applying the criterion of direct institution by Christ

Explain the Reformed teaching that baptism is administered once, that its efficacy is not tied to the moment it is administered, and that grace and salvation are not so bound to it that no one can be saved without it
Evaluate transubstantiation, the Lutheran view, and bare memorialism against the Reformed teaching on the Lord's Supper using Scripture and the confessions
Evaluate credobaptist and paedobaptist arguments concerning the proper recipients of baptism in light of the biblical covenants
Evaluate arguments concerning the mode of baptism and explain why the Westminster Confession holds that immersion is not necessary
Compose a catechetical explanation that presents baptism and the Lord's Supper as visible words of the gospel sealing God's covenant promises

changes: Kept and reworded the real competencies (signs, institution, meaning of baptism and the Supper, comparison, self-examination, spiritual presence, worthy receiving, means of grace, evaluating rival views, visible words). Dropped vague items such as 'Connect the sacraments to the covenant and the church' and the redundant 'Defend' objective, folding their content into sharper ones. Changed 'Apply self-examination' to describing what Scripture requires, so the objective is about knowledge and not inner experience. Added missing competencies: the institution narrative, the Trinitarian baptismal formula, Old Testament covenant signs, improving one's baptism, communion with one another, sacramental union, recipients of baptism, efficacy of the sacraments, why there are only two, baptism's once-for-all character and relation to salvation, and evaluation of baptism debates on recipients and mode. Standardized confession citations to full document names with numbers, added Heidelberg and Westminster Confession anchors, and replaced loose references with specific verse ranges.
